title: Russia: Doubling down in Ukraine – and against the West
gist: Former NZ diplomat Ian Hill argues Russia is betting on exhaustion: sustaining attritional battlefield pressure, escalating winter missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, stepping up grey-zone attacks on Europe, and engaging only performatively in US peace efforts. Ukraine's economy and finances are deteriorating, European support may weaken with populist gains, and Russia's 2027 budget lifts defence spending 27%.

insights.claim: Hopes that Ukraine's summer 2026 long-range drone attacks on Russian energy and other infrastructure would turn the tide of the war proved misplaced.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy have not been decisive, reducing odds of a near-term Russian capitulation.

insights.claim: Russia has been unable to seize the key 'fortress' cities of Slovyansk, Kramatorsk and Kostyantynivka in a drone-dominated war of attrition that offers little scope for dramatic advances.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Front lines remain largely static, prolonging the conflict.
insights.locator: Russia has been unable so far

insights.claim: Russia must recruit at least 30,000 new troops monthly to sustain heavy casualties, and growing difficulty with voluntary recruitment has prompted speculation of creeping mobilisation that the Kremlin would prefer to avoid for political and economic reasons.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Mobilisation would tighten Russia's labour market further and add economic strain.
insights.quote: Russia continues to sustain heavy casualties, requiring it to recruit at least 30,000 new troops monthly.
insights.locator: Russia continues to sustain heavy casualties

insights.claim: Ukraine faces substantial losses and a growing deficit in personnel and munitions relative to Russia.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Sustained demand for Western munitions production.
insights.locator: Russia continues to sustain heavy casualties

themes.theme: Winter air campaign on energy infrastructure

insights.claim: Using jet-propelled drones and ballistic missiles, Russia has sharply increased the frequency, volume and range of targets of its aerial attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Escalating strikes raise damage to Ukrainian energy and logistics assets.

insights.claim: Hill predicts Russia will intensify missile and drone attacks over winter to destroy Ukraine's key energy and logistics infrastructure and break civilian morale, especially in Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Expect Ukrainian power deficits and higher European energy import needs for Ukraine this winter.
insights.quote: Moscow wants to undermine civilian morale by making life intolerable, especially in Kyiv, thereby bringing the city to its knees.

insights.claim: Ukraine's ability to counter Russian air attacks is hampered by insufficient air defences, especially Patriot systems.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Persistent demand for Patriot and other air-defence systems supports defence contractors.
insights.locator: Ukraine’s efforts to counter these attacks

insights.claim: Ukraine's economy is floundering, with its steel industry at a standstill, grain exports through Black Sea ports cut off, and Kyiv seeking an advance on EU and IMF funding for 2027 as it runs out of money.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Loss of Ukrainian grain and steel exports affects global supply, and Ukraine's financing gap increases reliance on EU/IMF.

insights.claim: Signs of disunity within Ukraine's political elite are growing, aided by missteps from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, which Moscow will seek to exploit.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Political instability in Kyiv raises risk of unfavourable settlement terms.

themes.theme: Hybrid war on Europe and transatlantic wedge

insights.claim: Russia is expected to step up grey-zone actions in Europe — social media manipulation, political interference, cyber-attacks and sabotage — calibrated to avoid triggering NATO's Article V while eroding European support for Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Rising cyber and sabotage risk to European infrastructure and firms.
insights.locator: This may include social media manipulation

insights.claim: European support for Ukraine has held so far, but the rise of right- and left-wing populist parties, especially in France and Germany, suggests it may come under greater pressure in 2027.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: European political shifts are a key variable for Ukraine funding and sanctions durability.
insights.locator: So far, European support has held firm

insights.claim: Hill argues Russia's engagement in US-led peace efforts is essentially performative unless a settlement meets Moscow's core objectives, and Moscow is reportedly offering Washington bilateral commercial advantages to pressure Kyiv into a deal.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Ceasefire hopes priced into markets may be premature; watch for US-Russia commercial deals.
insights.quote: But there’s no real sign that Moscow is seriously interested yet in ending the fighting.

insights.claim: Hill argues war-weariness and economic strain in Russia will not constrain Putin, because public opinion can be managed or repressed and the economic problems are not severe enough to halt the war.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Economic pressure via sanctions is unlikely to force a near-term Russian settlement.
insights.locator: Grumbling (Opens in new window) in the Russian elite

insights.claim: Russia does not consider itself isolated, engaging with BRICS and Shanghai Cooperation Organisation partners including China and India while positioning itself as a leader of the 'Global Majority'.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Continued trade ties with China and India blunt Western sanctions' effectiveness.
insights.locator: Nor does Moscow consider itself isolated

insights.claim: Statements by Putin and Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov indicate Moscow remains committed to control over all of Donbas, a pliant government in Kyiv and Ukrainian neutrality.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Maximalist Russian aims make a negotiated settlement unlikely soon.

insights.claim: Russia's 2027 budget projects a 27% rise in defence spending, financed by cuts to health and education and a rising budget deficit.
insights.speaker: Ian Hill
insights.so_what: Militarised fiscal policy widens Russia's deficit and signals long-term confrontation with the West, supporting European rearmament.
insights.quote: Moscow’s 2027 budget projects a 27% rise in defence spending (Opens in new window).
